subject.title: [OAuth] Client ID revoked `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` - fresh ChatGPT Plus logins completely broken

question: Should OpenClaw rotate the built-in ChatGPT/Codex OAuth client ID, keep tracking upstream Codex's public client ID, or add an owner-approved override path?
rationale: The current source still uses the reported ID and the issue describes a severe auth setup blocker, but upstream Codex still uses the same ID and this review could not reproduce the `invalid_client` page without real account/browser proof.

options.title: Validate Then Rotate
options.body: Run a fresh-account browser OAuth proof and, if the client is invalid for OpenClaw, update every owned OAuth surface with an approved replacement client ID and regression proof.

options.title: Stay Upstream-Aligned
options.body: Keep the upstream Codex client ID if real-account validation shows the reported failure is not caused by revocation, then improve diagnostics for the actual failure mode.

options.title: Add Official Override
options.body: Introduce a documented maintainer-owned override only if OpenAI or deployment policy requires per-owner OAuth apps and the config-surface cost is accepted.

recommendation.title: Validate Then Rotate
recommendation.body: Run a fresh-account browser OAuth proof and, if the client is invalid for OpenClaw, update every owned OAuth surface with an approved replacement client ID and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current OpenAI provider identity and ChatGPT OAuth files came through the OpenAI unification PR history.
